$$a\cdot P = 54, \qquad a\cdot T = 117-15k.$$

Compute $6-k$ and $9-k$:
$$6-k=\frac{9(2T-P)}{5P},\qquad 9-k=\frac{6(P+3T)}{5P}.$$

Then $a=(6-k)(9-k)=\dfrac{54(2T-P)(P+3T)}{25P^2}$. Setting equal to $54/P$:

$$(2T-P)(P+3T)=25P.$$

Expanding: $-P^2-PT+6T^2=25P$, i.e.
$$P^2+(T+25)P-6T^2=0.$$

Discriminant in $P$: $(T+25)^2+24T^2=25\big((T+1)^2+24\big)$. For $P$ rational we need $(T+1)^2+24=m^2$, i.e.
$$(m-(T+1))(m+(T+1))=24.$$

Both factors have the same parity; since $24$ is even, both even. Enumerating even factor pairs of $24$:

| $(a,b)$ | $m$ | $T+1$ | $T$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $(2,12)$ | $7$ | $5$ | $4$ |

| $0$ | $0$ | — | invalid ($a$ undefined) | — |

$$3,\ \tfrac{33}{4},\ \tfrac{39}{5},\ 15,\ \tfrac{15}{2},\ \tfrac{21}{2},\ 7.$$

$$S=\left\{3,\ 6,\ 7,\ 9,\ 15,\ \tfrac{15}{2},\ \tfrac{21}{2},\ \tfrac{33}{4},\ \tfrac{39}{5}\right\}.$$

All nine values are distinct.

$$18+\dfrac{321}{20}=\dfrac{360+321}{20}=\dfrac{681}{20}.$$

$$\text{Sum}=40+\dfrac{681}{20}=\dfrac{800+681}{20}=\boxed{\dfrac{1481}{20}}.$$
